item.title: Michael Carrick has painfully awkward exchange with interviewer over Man United future
item.description: Michael Carrick endured an awkward end to a post-match interview as he had an excruciating exchange about his future as Manchester United manager. Carrick had just watched his United side fight back from 4-2 down in injury time to snatch the unlikeliest of 4-4 draws with Aston Villa , having earlier come back from being 2-0 behind inside five minutes. It was a real mixed display from the Red Devils, who showed plenty of heart and character but had put themselves in bad positions due to consistently disastrous defending. The result – combined with their incredible comeback victory against Roma in midweek – has probably saved Carrick’s job, although his United side still head into this international break in the Premier League ’s bottom three, lying 18th in the table. His long-term future appears to very much still be up in the air and his post-match interview on Sky Sports with reporter Patrick Davison was an awkward watch. Carrick firstly bristled slightly when asked if United are looking at a relegation fight, saying: “No, we’re in November. I don’t like this situation we’re in, I don’t like the results we’ve had but we can definitely do something about it.” "That's not going to happen" 🗣️ Michael Carrick responds to the notion that he could resign as Manchester United head coach 🔴 pic.twitter.com/q1fBKSXL7l — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) November 8, 2026 From there, things got worse, as Davison asked a lengthy question suggesting there were clearly going to be conversations about his future during the international break over the next couple of weeks, to which Carrick simply responded: "Is there?" When it was suggested that one would assume so, Carrick tersely said: “Would you?” and when he was pushed for what he thought about his situation, the Man United boss said to Davison: “You’re telling me, what do you think”. After that, the interviewer specified that he wanted to know what Carrick expected to happen in the next couple of weeks and he then gave a longer answer admitting that it wasn’t a good situation, the team haven’t won enough games but that he expects to move forward and keep working on the things they’ve been working on until this point. Michael Carrick (Reuters) Back in the Sky Sports studio, pundit Roy Keane was asked for his thoughts on the interview as a whole and the former Man United captain compared the current boss to a politician. He said: “It’s obviously difficult for the manager, he’s under pressure no doubt. He talks a lot but doesn’t say much – maybe that’s a tactic. He’s like a politician. “He’s clearly under pressure and says he knows there are things to work on but he better get moving on that... This is their worst start in however many years.”

item.title: Caleb Williams MVP Case Hinges On Sunday Night Against Tampa Bay
item.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images A Bears victory on Sunday could push Caleb Williams into the MVP conversation. That number trails Josh Allen, Brock Purdy, and Joe Burrow, but the gap is closing fast. Since Williams came back from a hamstring injury that sidelined him during Weeks 3 through 5, the Bears have claimed three consecutive victories. Chicago has not trailed in any of those three contests and has scored more than 30 points each time. Williams has fixed the biggest issue from his rookie year. His completion percentage has jumped from 58.1 percent in 2025 to 70.9 percent this season. Yahoo Sports noted that only Joe Burrow holds a higher rate in the entire league. At Halas Hall on Wednesday, Coach Ben Johnson informed reporters that the passing operation feels much smoother. “I think our passing game in general has been a little bit cleaner,” Johnson said. Enhanced timing and confidence linking the quarterback with his leading trio of receivers fuel this progress. The Chemistry Is Real The connection between Williams and his targets has deepened beyond the field. The group spends significant time together to build that bond. Williams explained that the communication grew because they share meals and hang out. “We hang out together. We do things together. We eat together, break bread together,” Williams said. Luther Burden III showed this grit against Seattle by catching a 1-yard touchdown to end an 8-minute, 32-second opening drive. Before the catch, Burden told Williams he did not fear the defending Super Bowl champions. “I went up to him and told him I don’t care who they is,” the wide receiver said. Williams stood up from the bench and yelled back, “I don’t give a f— who they are!” Blocking Wins Games Too The offense also relies on the receivers to do the dirty work. Rome Odunze is the key player in this new dynamic. He cleared a path for a 39-yard screen pass against Seattle that sealed the win. Kalif Raymond ran through the tunnel because Odunze made the block. “If [Odunze] doesn’t get that block, the screen doesn’t go,” Raymond said. With 14 receptions totaling 234 yards in each half, Odunze is heading toward his finest campaign in three years. On Sunday, Nov. 8, at 8:20 p.m. ET, they face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field. TSN noted that Tampa Bay yields just 18.9 points per game, which is the fifth-best mark in the league.

item.title: Inter player ratings vs Como: Marcus Thuram leads the charge in commanding San Siro victory
item.description: FC Internazionale v Como 1907 - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Inter Milan produced a clinical first-half display to secure a 2-0 victory over Como at the Giuseppe Meazza. Goals from Francesco Esposito and Marcus Thuram proved decisive in a match where the hosts efficiently managed their lead. Inter Milan demonstrated their tactical superiority at San Siro, securing a controlled 2-0 victory over a resilient Como side. The Nerazzurri wasted no time asserting their authority, with Francesco Esposito breaking the deadlock in the 12th minute following excellent work by Djed Spence. The pressure remained relentless, and just seven minutes later, Marcus Thuram doubled the advantage, effectively settling the contest before the twenty-minute mark. Inter's ability to compress the pitch in the middle third stifled Como's build-up play, limiting the visitors to just a single shot on target throughout the ninety minutes. Despite Como enjoying more of the ball in the second half (57% total possession), Inter remained the more dangerous side on the counter, racking up an expected goals (xG) value of 1.86 compared to the visitors' 0.20. Cristian Chivu’s side displayed impressive defensive discipline, recorded 12 interceptions and winning the majority of their physical duels. While the intensity naturally dipped after the interval, the damage done in the opening exchange ensured a comfortable evening for the reigning giants, moving them closer to the summit of the Serie A table. Goalkeeper & Defence Josep Martinez - 7/10 A largely spectator role for the Spanish goalkeeper, who was only required to make one save all afternoon. His distribution was efficient, helping Inter bypass Como's initial press, and he commanded his area well during the few crosses that bypassed the front line. Alessandro Bastoni - 7/10 Typically progressive in his passing, Bastoni acted as a secondary playmaker from the left side of the back three. He remained untroubled defensively and was key to the clean sheet, contributing to a defensive unit that allowed very little central penetration. Manuel Akanji - 7/10 The Swiss international provided the structural security Inter needed in the heart of the defence. His positioning was immaculate, ensuring that Douvikas was starved of service, and he handled the physical transitions with his usual composure. Carlos Augusto - 7/10 Slotting into the back three, Augusto showed his versatility. He was quick to cover the space behind Dimarco and was proactive in his defensive duties, helping Inter maintain their 12 interceptions as a team. Midfield Federico Dimarco - 7/10 A constant threat down the left flank until his substitution in the 87th minute. His delivery from wide areas remained a primary weapon for Inter, and his tactical discipline in tracking back prevented Yago Couto from finding any joy in the final third. Djed Spence - 8/10 An excellent performance from the wing-back, who provided the assist for the opening goal in the 12th minute

item.title: Braden Mann unleashes an 85-yard punt for Eagles
item.description: Sunday’s game against the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles has been something of a defensive struggle. So when Nick Sirianni sent Braden Mann and the rest of the Philadelphia punt team into the game with under 30 seconds left in the first half, leading 8-6 but deep in their own territory, Sirianni probably just wanted to try and get his defense into better field position. He likely did not expect Mann to pin the Giants inside New York’s own 10-yard line. But that is exactly what happened, as Mann unleashed a booming 85-yard punt that rolled out of bounds at the Giants’ 6-yard line: BRADEN MANN WHAT A PUNT NYGvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0knmQEiDKM — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 The massive punt sent FOX Sports announced Joe Davis into a state of delirium, as he declared that the kick had to be “close to the longest punt in NFL history.’ Interestingly enough, however, it does not even crack the top ten! According to Pro Football Reference, the longest punt in NFL history remains this booming 98-yard punt from Steve O’Neal of the New York Jets, back in 1969. A 92-yard punt from Shawn McCarthy of the New England Patriots comes in second, while the legendary kick from Randall Cunningham of the 1989 Eagles, which covered 91 yards, comes in third. Sammy Baugh’s 1940 punt of 85 yards comes in at No. 12 on the list, which is the mark Mann tied with this kick. You can see that full list here .

item.title: Jorge Martin will be "almost 100% fit" in Portugal as heroic Qatar display keeps title hopes alive
item.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin , who finished seventh in Sunday's MotoGP race at Lusail, showcased his trademark resilience throughout the weekend in Qatar. Resilience that saw him go from considering skipping the race entirely early in the week to not only competing but delaying Marc Marquez's title celebrations. Once again, MotoGP's Asian flyaway races have proven decisive in the outcome of the world championship, which is now firmly within Marquez's grasp. The Ducati rider could be crowned champion in two weeks' time, but that he failed to seal the title in Qatar was thanks to Marco Bezzecchi's speed and Martin's resilience. Read Also: MotoGP Qatar GP: Marco Bezzecchi wins as Marc Marquez has title triumph delayed Over the course of this week, Martin went from contemplating staying in Spain and missing the race at Lusail, because of the pain caused by the fracture in his right wrist, to finishing third in Saturday's sprint and seventh in Sunday's grand prix. Despite losing further ground to Marquez, the Aprilia rider demonstrated a remarkable ability to endure pain, earning praise from most of his rivals. His achievement was all the more impressive considering he started from 11th on the grid - 10th on Sunday after Francesco Bagnaia 's withdrawal - which made his task even more difficult and increased the level of risk he had to take. "I'm proud of what I've done because on Monday and Tuesday I didn't even want to come here, and in the end I managed to finish both races," said Martin in his Spanish interview on Sunday evening. "We're going to Portugal still in with a chance. It's getting harder and harder, but we're still there." Although the injury is less serious than initially feared, the limitations it imposes on him when changing direction and braking are evident, particularly over a long run or race. Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team "I can't ride properly, I can't brake properly and I can't push the bike to the limit. It was really tough towards the end. For the last three laps, I just wanted the race to be over." In the sprint, Martin benefited from his last-minute decision to use the soft rear tyre, which allowed him to gain several positions through the opening corners. On Sunday, with everyone running the same tyre specification, the playing field was more level. "There was a lot of risk in the opening corners. The key was qualifying, because starting so far back didn't help me," explained the #89, who was physically exhausted by the end of the race. "My hand is swollen up like a melon, but I think I'll be almost 100% fit in Portugal. I'm tough and stubborn. There's something inside me that keeps pushing me to fight," concluded Martin, who will head to the Algarve circuit 60 points behind Marquez and 14 ahead of Bezzecchi. item.title: Ninkovich Unloads Brutal Truth: Kelce Is Just A Receiver
item.description: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images Rob Ninkovich delivered a sharp critique of Travis Kelce during the Hall of Fame induction ceremony for Rob Gronkowski at Gillette Stadium on Saturday. The former New England Patriots linebacker stated clearly that Kelce does not measure up to Gronkowski in the eyes of those who value the blocking aspect of the position. Ninkovich attended the event where Gronkowski received his red jacket and joined the 38th member of the Patriots Hall of Fame. The comments came while Ninkovich was asked to compare the two stars who have dominated the tight end position in recent years. He did not hold back his opinion about the Kansas City Chiefs star versus the New England legend. The debate centers on what defines a complete tight end in the NFL. Ninkovich believes that receiving ability alone is not enough to claim the title of the greatest. He pointed out that Gronkowski brought a physical element to the game that Kelce has not shown in the same way. This view was shared by many fans and analysts who remember the physical play of the former Patriots star. The ceremony was a celebration of Gronkowski’s nine seasons in New England, but the comparison to his successor in popularity sparked a new discussion about the position. Ninkovich’s words were direct and focused on the specific skills required to play the role as he sees it. Ninkovich Draws a Hard Line Between the Two Stars Rob Ninkovich made his stance clear when he addressed the comparison between Travis Kelce and Rob Gronkowski during the induction speech. He told the crowd that the two players are not similar in their approach to the game. Ninkovich stated, “Kelce and [Rob Gronkowski] don’t even come close. He’s [Kelce] a receiver. This guy’s [Gronkowski] a tight end,” according to Yahoo Sports . This comment highlights the former Patriots linebacker’s belief that the definition of the position includes more than just catching passes. He sees Gronkowski as the standard for what a tight end should be because of his willingness to engage in the trenches. The former linebacker has questioned Kelce’s blocking ability before this event took place. Ninkovich recalled facing the Chiefs star during his playing days and suggested that Kelce’s approach to the position was incomplete. He shared a specific memory from the field to support his argument. “I mean, I’ve played against Kelce, and I’ve thrown him around like he’s a little doll,” he said, as reported by Yahoo Sports. This anecdote is the foundation for his claim that Kelce lacks the physical dominance required to be considered a true tight end in the traditional sense. item.title: Match review: RSL secures 6th consecutive playoff berth in 2-1 victory over LA
item.description: Sergi Solans (22) celebrates after notching his third MLS brace and 14th goal of his rookie season. | Real Salt Lake Real Salt Lake secured a 2-1 victory and a spot in the MLS Playoffs in the high-stakes, must-win Decision Day matchup against the LA Galaxy in front of a roaring crowd of 20,738 fans at America First Field. Solans and Booth lift RSL to playoff berth Spanish sensation Sergi Solans continued his impressive rookie MLS campaign, netting his 15th goal in the 10th minute to give RSL the early lead, putting him just two goals shy of the MLS rookie regular season scoring record of 17 goals (Cyle Larin in 2015 with Orlando City SC). The scoring continued with Utah native Zach Booth netting his second goal of the 2026 season just two minutes later. With the Decision Day victory, Real Salt Lake has officially punched its ticket to the postseason for a sixth consecutive season, the longest active playoff streak in the Western Conference. Although the evening was a nail biter the home side further cemented itself as a constant within the best squads in the Western Conference, earning ninth place and a spot in the Wild Card match. Quotable “We could only do what we could, which was win the game and then the universe had to do its thing, it’s gotta cook. We were in the right spot to receive its blessings and all we talked about was controlling what we can, and tonight the guys did a great job.“ — RSL coach Pablo Mastroeni Game summary The Claret-and-Cobalt opened up the Decision Day battle with energy, pushing up the pitch immediately as Solans and Canadian defender Luc de Fougerolles each earned tangible scoring opportunities in the second and fifth minutes. Although the early momentum continued with the home side netting two goals within minutes of each other, the LA Galaxy found the back of the net in the 40th minute to make the score 2-1. After earning an impressive seven shots on target, Real Salt Lake headed into the locker room with a one goal lead. The home side continued to show grit and energy as the second half began, stringing together passes to bring the ball up the pitch and into its attacking third. In the 59th minute, RSL Head coach Pablo Mastroeni made his first substitutions of the match bringing on defensive veterans DeAndre Yedlin and Justen Glad. Mastroeni’s men worked as a unit to thwart multiple attacks by the Galaxy throughout the second half to secure the ever important victory. The win catapulted the squad into ninth place and earned the home side a spot in the wild card. Up next Real Salt Lake will now face the Seattle Sounders in the Wild Card match on Nov. 19th. With a win, the squad will face the top seeded Vancouver Whitecaps in a best-of-three set of matches. Kickoff for the Wild Card matchup is slated to kickoff at 8 p.m. MDT and will be streaming on Apple TV.

item.title: “I’m so tired”: Matheus Cunha dismayed by Man United’s weak mentality that cost them a win vs Aston Villa
item.description: “I’m so tired”: Matheus Cunha dismayed by Man United’s weak mentality that cost them a win vs Aston Villa Manchester United came back from two goals down in each half to eventually clinch a point after a thrilling tie against Aston Villa on Sunday. The visitors scored twice within the first five minutes of the first half and then scored another two within the opening eight minutes of the restart. On both occasions, the Red Devils managed to claw their way back, with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans scoring in the first 45 minutes before substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu combined in added time to ensure the game finished 4-4. Will it be enough for Michael Carrick to remain at the helm? Only time will tell, but as most fans inside Old Trafford saw, the mistakes of key players let him down once again. Matheus Cunha cannot believe the weak mentality on show Diogo Dalot was at fault for two of those goals, and how the Portuguese defender has remained at the club for so long is beyond puzzling at this point. Matheus Cunha, who won the first penalty, was candid in his assessment after the game, revealing that he was tired of the way the team performed tonight. United only seemed to wake up after conceding and not from the start, and that mentality needs to change immediately, as this style of play is simply unsustainable. “I’m so tired and also disappointed. After the other night we talked about how we concede goals and have the mentality to come back in the game. Time for major changes “We did it again where we had to play like Manchester United and go forward. We showed courage but we only do this after we concede goals: showed character after conceding goals. “If we had shown that character and courage before then we will win more games. I don’t know why we are making it hard for ourselves. “We all work hard and we all want to be the best. We need to change our mentality from the beginning.” No wonder everyone wanted INEOS to strengthen the backline in the summer. Hopefully, they finally heed the call in January. item.title: Cowboys Scheme Leaves Defensive Backs Blind To Ball
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys secondary has gone months without a single interception by a defensive back. The unit features high-priced players and a deep roster. On Nov. 17, 2025, safety Markquese Bell secured the last interception by a Cowboys safety. That date feels like ancient history in a season that has already slipped away. The only three picks the team has this year belong to linebackers Shemar James, DeMarvion Overshown, and Dee Winters. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker told Yahoo Sports exactly why the corners and safeties are stuck in neutral. He said, “I think that just has to do with No. 1 you’re dictating coverage so you can find the ball.” Parker admitted the scheme forces defensive backs into man-to-man coverage where they cannot see the quarterback’s eyes. He added, “I mean, I think it’s as simple as that.” The team tries to use match-zone coverage, but the execution keeps them from finding the ball in the air. The Cost of Man Coverage When you force corners to play tight man coverage, you give up yards. Cornerback DaRon Bland leads the team with six pass breakups, but he has also allowed an NFL-high 438 yards. Quarterbacks have thrown for three touchdowns against him with a rating of 117.4. Parker acknowledged the issue directly. “Yeah, and we need more from him,” Parker said. He noted that Bland has been close on many contested catches but needs to finish the plays. The problem is that one mistake in the secondary puts the whole defense in the spotlight. If the linebackers are supposed to have the vision, why are the defensive backs getting burned? Parker said the linebackers play with more vision because they are in zone. Meanwhile, the corners and safeties are locked in man coverage. This leaves them blind to the quarterback’s progressions until it is too late. A Drought That Hurts the Season The Cowboys are sitting at 3-5 after losing to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime on Sunday, Nov. 1. The loss came after the team let a 24-10 lead slip away in the fourth quarter. Dak Prescott never threw a pass on the final drive after an onside kick recovery. He took a sack and watched Javonte Williams run for three yards on third-and-16. Prescott said, “Maybe the drive after the onside kick,” and called it the turning point. But the defense cannot help the offense if they cannot take the ball away. Defensive lineman Quinnen Williams called out the unit for their lack of execution. “We’re the problem. We’re the reason why we’re losing these games,” he said. Dallas opponents succeed on 51.4% of their third-down attempts. The Colts, who Dallas faces on Sunday, Nov. 8, will exploit this weakness. If the scheme does not change, the secondary will continue to give up big plays.

item.title: Jason Kelce breaks down ‘really important’ Chiefs vs Jets moment Justin Fields got wrong
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Justin Fields saw rare action for the Kansas City Chiefs. It did not go as planned. Former New York Jets quarterback Justin Fields has been patiently waiting for a chance. And when you are sitting behind Patrick Mahomes, that does not happen very often. The Chiefs drew up a play for Fields against his former team, bringing him in to attempt a quarterback sneak. Unfortunately he failed to execute, with the Jets stopping him short and recovering the ball for a fumble. Jason Kelce gives verdict on Justin Fields fumble A key factor for any quarterback entering the game is his chemistry with his offensive line. And this was part of where it all went wrong. Former NFL star Jason Kelce pointed to the snap from Chiefs center Creed Humphrey, noting that this started the play badly. Kelce wrote on X : “Center QB exchange is really important for QB sneak, and often overlooked. Because of the way the Center fires off the ball, the Quarterback, or whoever is taking the snap needs to get reps full speed of the snap from the center in practice to get an accurate feel.” But this does not absolve Fields from blame. Kelce noted that the backup quarterback may have got his timing all wrong. “There’s also a timing to it from the QB, not sure how many Fields has done, but he looked like he moved quickly before securing the snap there. “I like that KC is finally running it, but an unfortunate start. There’s more nuance to that play than people realize.” In the opening eight weeks of the NFL season, Justin Fields did not take a single snap. And he really needed to make this one count. A fan wrote on X: “The QB sneak/tush push with Justin Fields went so well I expect Andy Reid won’t call it again for the rest of his life.” There will be plenty for Reid and his staff to analyze on this play in the film room on Monday. Fields will just need to pray that he gets another chance. item.title: Briscoe Takes Pole As Homestead Finale Sets Stage For Title Showdown
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Chase Briscoe secured the pole position for the NASCAR Cup Series season finale, putting Joe Gibbs Racing ahead before the green flag drops on Sunday. The No. 19 Toyota driver posted a lap of 166.687 mph to edge his teammate Denny Hamlin by a razor-thin 0.017 seconds, per Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup. The result follows a year in which the team often struggled in qualifying, and Briscoe secured the win at a crucial moment. The 267-lap race at Homestead-Miami Speedway will decide the 2026 champion, and starting from the front row is the best possible spot to control the pace. A Tight Pack for the Title Three drivers remain in the championship battle, and their starting spots are closely grouped. According to Motorsport.com NASCAR Cup, Kyle Larson, who leads the points, will start fourth and requires only eight stage points to secure his third title. His closest rival, Christopher Bell, qualified sixth and trails by 67 points. Denny Hamlin is second on the front row but faces a steep climb, 70 points behind Larson with 76 points available in the race. Briscoe, who is out of title contention, stated “Yeah, our car was really good yesterday in practice too,” when discussing the speed his team found on Friday. Hamlin admitted he lost the pole by “trying to save the tires a little bit too much coming to the green,” which cost him the top spot by a fraction of a second. Brad Keselowski’s Final Bow The starting grid also marks a sad end for Brad Keselowski in his final race as a driver and co-owner for RFK Racing. Keselowski lost control of his car at the exit of Turn 4 during qualifying and spun into the inside wall, leaving him starting in the 40th and final position. “The track’s really, really slick,” said Keselowski afterward, explaining the difficult conditions that led to his crash. He added that he “Was trying to find a place that had some grip” but simply could not find it, noting, “Wish i could have that one back, but just trying to find something to be as fast as i could be.” His misfortune highlights the unforgiving nature of the 1.5-mile oval where grip is scarce. Sunday, Nov. 8, at 3 p.m. is the scheduled time for the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship race.

item.title: Bears Must Target Cornerback Riq Woolen Over Chase Young
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears face a critical choice before the trade deadline. While chatter swirls around a potential reunion with Khalil Mack or a move for Chase Young, the real need lies in the secondary. Due to a thumb injury sustained during the Week 8 victory, the team has just placed running back Zavier Scott on injured reserve. Scott will miss at least four games, leaving the depth chart thin. The current roster cannot afford to ignore the pass coverage holes. Why the Secondary Takes Priority Many fans want a big edge rusher to help the pass rush. However, league evaluators have shifted their view on what the team actually lacks. On Wednesday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that the Bears have been linked to edge-rushers such as Khalil Mack, but a few league evaluators told him that cornerback is becoming more of a need. Adding another pass-rusher does not fix the leaks in the coverage unit. The offense has been strong, rushing for 1,206 yards through eight games. The defense must match that energy to keep Caleb Williams off the field. The Case for Woolen Over Young Reports indicate the Bears have checked in on Saints defensive end Chase Young. The NFL Rumors X account shared that the Bears and 49ers have checked in on the Saints’ Chase Young. While Young has stats to back him up, he is not the right fit for this specific roster gap. The team is also in deep competition with the Lions to acquire Riq Woolen from the Eagles. Thomas R. Petersen reported via X on Thursday that they are reportedly in deep competition with Lions to acquire Riq Woolen from the Eagles. Woolen offers a one-year solution that fits the cap and the timeline. Jacob Infante of Windy City Gridiron wrote that given the fact that Woolen is only a one-year rental, it would be surprising to see him cost more than a Day 3 draft pick. This low cost makes him a smart target compared to the high price of Young. The Window Is Closing Fast The Bears have shown they are willing to spend draft capital to win now. They already sent two first-round picks to land Jeffery Simmons. Brad Briggs added context on the injury front, noting it’s actually a thumb injury for Zavier Scott, and there is reason for hope that his stay on injured reserve will be on the shorter side. Even with that hope, the immediate void remains. The team must act to secure Woolen before the Lions steal him away. The next game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday starts the clock on this decision.

Their sixth win in seven Premier League matches was enough to move them above Manchester City, who suffered a shock 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest less than 24 hours earlier, and underline their position as the closest challengers to leaders Arsenal. With a five-point gap to the Gunners, that is certainly the case for now, although Brighton's influential midfielder Pascal Gross was reluctant to entertain such talk at this stage. "No, we are not in a title race," the 35-year-old told Sky Sports after Sunday's success. "But we have started the season really well. It's the beginning of the season. "You see the Premier League, the margins and you look at the results - we are not getting carried away yet. "Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum, but we are really pleased to head into the international break like this." But 10 years on from Leicester City's title triumph against all odds, could they really achieve the impossible and win the Premier League? 'The football they're playing is outstanding' As each week passes, though, it is becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss Brighton's credentials. Having won seven of their opening 10 Premier League matches, including beating Arsenal and Manchester City, the Seagulls have shown quality as well as character. item.title: Lando Norris goes viral after Brazilian GP podium celebration goes wrong
item.description: Motorsport photo Lando Norris has gone viral on social media after his Brazilian Grand Prix podium mishap. The McLaren driver controlled almost everything that came his way at Interlagos, right up until he got to the podium. The 2025 champion went for his usual party trick after collecting his trophy, crouching down and slamming the base of the champagne bottle onto the ground to send the contents fizzing out the top. But this time, the bottle gave way on impact and smashed on the floor. He then stepped forward and appeared to be hit in the face by the podium fireworks. Norris did not seem to be hurt by the incident and was seen laughing it off with Red Bull drivers Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar , who had finished second and third, respectively. The moment quickly went viral on social media. "Broke the bottle, walked into the fireworks. Not a win he'll forget easily," one fan commented on Reddit, while another added: "Next race they'll hand him a participation certificate printed on laminated paper." "Another Lando classic moment on the podium," someone else posted, while another wrote: "Destroyed the bottle with a pretty majestic slam... and then put his head inside a flowing firework stream. That's gotta be worth at least one extra point or something haha." Further reactions included: "Classic Lando on the podium shenanigans" and "This was hilarious. Breaks the bottle, takes the pyrotechnics to the face, and is then immediately sprayed by all three of them while dying of embarrassment." Norris has celebrated this way since his junior racing days, and he explained how it works on the F1 Explains podcast last year. "Instead of shaking the bottle and then spraying it, you smash it against the ground," he said. "The trick here is to not smash it. And the trick to that is by having a very, very thick, strong bottle." The mishap did not take much of the shine off Norris's afternoon. He beat Verstappen by 14.602 seconds in changing conditions to take his third win of the season, with Hadjar completing the podium in third. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Ipswich Town to save Suffolk Punch horse charity
item.description: The Suffolk Punch has featured on Ipswich Town's crest since 1972, based on a design by John Gammage [ITFC] A charity which protects the critically endangered Suffolk Punch horse breed is to be saved by Ipswich Town FC. The horse has featured on the club's badge for more than 50 years and news the Suffolk Punch Trust may soon cease to exist hit fans hard. The trust closed its visitor centre, cafe and shop due to high costs in February and later put its 120-acre farm and visitor centre on the market for £2.4m . "We carry the Suffolk Punch on our crest... and this has been one that people have been keen for us to support and it's the right thing to do," said Mark Ashton, chairman and chief executive of the Premier League side. "Whatever football club you support, you know what the Suffolk Punch means and you know what club it represents, so I think it's important - numerous supporters have written to me about this." The announcement was made in an interview on BBC Radio Suffolk just prior to kick-off, ahead of commentary on the Tractor Boys' 2-1 defeat to Bournemouth . Suffolk Punch horses – including award-winning show horses - have been bred at the trust's Colony Stud at Hollesley, on the Suffolk coast, since 1759. According to its website, the site is home to its own 19 horses, so the sale raised questions about what would happen to them. Credit: Annabelle Gordon - Pool/Getty NEED TO KNOW Melania Trump attended a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Alabama on Nov. 7 The first lady was met with a mix of boos and cheers, video shared online shows Trump’s attendance at the sporting event came after the White House announced she had secured a $7.2 million scholarship endowment for LSU through her Fostering the Future initiative Melania Trump was met with a mixed reaction while attending a Louisiana State University (LSU) football game this weekend. The first lady, 56, was in attendance as the LSU Tigers went up against the University of Alabama’s Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., on Saturday, Nov. 7. At one point, when Trump’s face appeared on the stadium’s Jumbotron while an announcer welcomed her to the game, the crowd could be heard both booing and cheering, videos shared on social media show . item.title: Legendary Steeler recognized as team’s Salute to Service nominee
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Former Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman Jon Kolb, left , shakes hands with team chairman Dan Rooney during a ceremony noting the Steelers holding NFL football training camps at Saint Vincent College in Latrobe, Pa. on Sunday, July 26, 2015 . (AP Photo/Keith Srakocic) Keith Srakocic A legendary Pittsburgh Steelers offensive lineman is the team’s nominee for the 2026 Salute to Service Award. Jon Kolb, an Army National Guard veteran, was selected for his work with Adventures in Training with a Purpose, a non-profit organization he founded to support veterans. Adventures in Training with a Purpose focuses on improving the lives of military members, veterans and first responders through targeted physical training. The organization provides services free of charge to help clients regain physical movement and carry out daily tasks independently. Steelers Vice President of Strategy Dan Rooney commended Kolb’s ongoing impact on the military community. “We selected Jon to represent the Steelers because his work with ATP reflects the value we place on supporting our military community,” Rooney said. “Through ATP, Jon combines his master’s degree in exercise science with the extensive strength and conditioning knowledge he developed as a professional athlete to make a meaningful difference in the lives of others. We applaud his leadership and dedication to helping service members, veterans and first responders improve their health and quality of life.” Kolb expressed gratitude for the recognition. “It is an honor to be nominated for doing work that I am so passionate about,” Kolb said. “There are individuals who, in many ways, feel trapped by their own bodies because they no longer have the freedom to move. Through ATP, we help give them their freedom back, often making a life-changing difference in their circumstances, independence and overall quality of life. It is incredibly rewarding to be able to make that kind of impact, especially for members of the military community.” The annual award recognizes NFL players, coaches, staff and alumni who demonstrate an exceptional commitment to supporting military members, veterans and their families. Kolb is one of 32 nominees. Fans can vote for nominees online through Nov. 30, with a limit of one vote per nominee per day. Fan voting will help determine three finalists, who will be announced in January 2027. The recipient will be recognized during Super Bowl LXI week in Los Angeles at NFL Honors, the league’s annual primetime awards special. USAA will contribute $25,000 in the award recipient’s name to official aid societies representing all U.S. military branches. The NFL Foundation will match USAA’s donation with an additional $25,000 contribution to the recipient’s military non-profit charity of choice. item.title: Freiburg third after beating Union, Leverkusen beat Cologne in derby
item.description: Freiburg's Japanese midfielder Yuito Suzuki scored in his side's 2-0 win over Union Berlin on Sunday. (Silas Stein) Freiburg kept hot on the heels of Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund with a comfortable 2-0 home win over lowly Union Berlin to return to third in the Bundesliga table on Sunday, while Bayer Leverkusen sunk derby rivals Cologne. Freiburg pressured Union captain Rani Khedira into an own goal nine minutes after half-time and Yuito Suzuki scored another as the hosts won despite their own skipper Vincenzo Grifo missing a penalty. Last season's beaten Europa League finalists are third on 19 points, two behind Bayern and Dortmund with the Bavarians ahead on goal difference. "We knew our chances would come and we managed to convert them well," Freiburg winger Derry Scherhant told DAZN. After an even first-half, Freiburg were impressive after the break and forced a last-ditch intervention from Khedira, who knocked the ball into his own net. Scherhant chipped for Suzuki to score with 67 minutes gone. The Black Forest side may have won by a higher margin were it not for Union goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow, who kept out Grifo's 84th-minute penalty and made a number of other saves. Earlier on Sunday, goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne which lifted the visitors to fifth in the table. The fiery encounter produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the home side. One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart. The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated. Leverkusen broke the deadlock just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on. Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide. Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half. Schick had a goal ruled out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league appearances this season. Germany winger Said El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback and left the hosts stranded in 15th, two points above Union who sit in the relegation play-off spot. dwi/ea/td

item.title: Chapman And Whitlock Anchor Red Sox Bullpen For 2027
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Boston Red Sox have a clear plan for the 2027 season, and it starts with two dominant arms. Aroldis Chapman and Garrett Whitlock will lead the bullpen again after a historic 2026 run. This is not a hopeful guess. The numbers prove it, and the money is already set. Per Yahoo Sports , the pair allowed just 21 earned runs over 104 innings to post a 1.82 ERA. Chapman turned 38 and still dominated the league. He posted a 1.92 ERA in 51.2 innings, which ranked as the 10th-lowest mark among all qualified relievers. His 35 saves were the fifth-most in baseball. He also became the all-time reliever strikeout king, passing Hall of Famer Hoyt Wilhelm. Chapman now sits ninth on the all-time saves list with 402 career saves. Chapman exercised his 2027 option worth $13 million after pitching over 40 innings and clearing his year-end physical. This deal locks in the best closer in the game. The Setup Man Is Just as Critical Garrett Whitlock does the heavy lifting before Chapman enters the game. Among 143 qualified relievers, his 1.72 ERA from 54 regular-season outings ranked sixth-lowest. With 2.73 in win probability added, Whitlock placed 12th across all relievers. His role is to set the table for Chapman, and he does it better than almost anyone else. Since Whitlock’s 2027 option was picked up, the Red Sox are likely to keep most of their bullpen for next season. The front office made the right call to keep this core together. Beyond the Top Two The rest of the unit looks solid too, even if the spotlight stays on the top two. After skipping major league action since 2019, 35-year-old Tanner Guerrero became one of baseball’s top relievers for much of 2026. In 40.2 innings, Guerrero posted a 3.10 ERA. He provides a necessary bridge that keeps the score low before the final inning. The depth here is rare in modern baseball. Unless something unexpected occurs, this duo will return in 2027 as one of the sport’s premier bullpen pairs. In 2026, the Red Sox bullpen recorded a 3.00 ERA, which was the best figure in baseball.

item.title: Man United’s unique comeback leaves no one knowing how to feel
item.description: As the Manchester United players who had been told they were not fit to wear the shirt, in perhaps the earliest ever airing of that chant in footballing history, celebrated a second ridiculous comeback in five days, the Stretford End launched into a different chorus. They had told the team they were unworthy of representing them after a mere five minutes, had cheered in damning fashion when the dreadful Diogo Dalot was substituted, had been vitriolic about the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. But United left the pitch in the relegation zone while their supporters serenaded Michael Carrick . “It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes,” they sang. In one respect, it was hard to believe it was not Sir Alex Ferguson , plucking results from nowhere. In another, it was hard to believe this was not the prelude to a sacking. Patrick Dorgu popped up to score an extraordinary stoppage-time equaliser (Reuters) It may still be. United have one win in 11 games, one point in three in the Premier League but Carrick is starting to specialise in escapology. Bournemouth had seemed the end for him, Roma looked it when his side were 2-0 down. Aston Villa seemed his valedictory game twice, before two two-goal comebacks. His team talks seem to backfire horribly and yet his side have twice delivered a show of spirit to salvage something from the brink of humiliation. Ferguson’s most famous comeback was delivered by two substitutes, Teddy Sheringham and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. If Carrick has a lifeline now, it came from two replacements, scorers in Fergie Time, when it seemed time had run out for the latest United manager. First Patrick Dorgu set up Joshua Zirkzee to halve the deficit. Then Dorgu headed in Bruno Fernandes ’ 96th-minute corner. A few minutes earlier, the Aston Villa supporters had been taunting their former midfielder Youri Tielemans with a chorus of: “Youri, what’s the score?” Few foresaw the eventual answer.
